chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from al-Kāhilī, who said:
I asked him about tayammum. He said: He struck the mat with his hand, then wiped his face with it, then wiped his two palms, one of them over the back of the other.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) in certain circumstances
key_terms.الْبِسَاطِ: the mat or spread upon which the hand was struck
key_terms.ظَهْرِ: the back side of the hand
key_terms.فَضَرَبَ: he struck or placed the hand upon a surface as part of the tayammum act
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, which is wiped in tayammum

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of performing tayammum through a practical demonstration. It shows striking a surface, wiping the face, and then wiping the hands, indicating a concise legal form for ritual purification when tayammum is required.
